claims: For two same-direction equal-input CPMM intents, processing the higher-minOut intent first maximizes executed input volume against the reverse order.
A satisfiable intent on a depleted pool is satisfiable on the original pool.
With equal inputs, both execution orders produce the same final depleted pool when both execute.
Total output is order-invariant for two equal-input intents when both execute.
The exchange property is sharp: it can fail without equal input sizes.
Position output is non-increasing through repeated equal-input execution, supporting the k-intent extension.
proof_method: CPMM output monotonicity and diminishing returns
native witnesses for sharpness and non-vacuity

boundaries: The main optimality theorem covers two same-direction intents with equal input sizes on one CPMM pool.
